product: Avast consumer security (Free Antivirus / Avast One), German site avast.com/de-de
vendor: Avast (brand of Gen Digital Inc.; operating entity Avast Software s.r.o., Prague)
summary: Avast is a real, financially backed and technically well-rated antivirus, owned by Gen Digital. Two final regulator decisions in 2024, from the FTC and the Czech DPA, found it sold or transferred re-identifiable browsing data of users via Jumpshot while telling users the data was anonymous. For a privacy and security vendor this contradicts its core promise. Under the rubric it stays RED despite the settlement, the payment and the passage of time. Continuing Dutch and UK claims add to the concern. Technical quality and finances are strong, and the data practice was stopped in 2020.
green_flags: Parent Gen Digital is profitable, with about $5B FY26 revenue [E5].
Patched CVEs and no breach found [E8].
yellow_flags: Dutch and UK civil claims over browsing data are ongoing [E4].
Overlapping SKUs and the Avast One repackaging make licensing unclear [E11].
Gen Digital's multi-brand portfolio makes consolidation possible [E6].
red_flags: The FTC final order (June 2024) found Avast and Jumpshot sold re-identifiable browsing data. It required a $16.5M payment and banned selling browsing data for advertising [E1].
The Czech DPA's final GDPR decision (April 2024) fined Avast CZK 351M for transferring non-anonymised browsing data of about 100M users to Jumpshot [E2].
reasoning:
Two independent final regulator findings establish the vendor's own misconduct: monetising user browsing data, with deceptive anonymity claims, in a privacy and security product. The rubric says such findings stay RED after settlement. The mitigating facts are the cessation of Jumpshot in 2020, the compliance order, the strong parent and the good detection results. Those do not remove the trust problem. Confidence is MEDIUM because the vendor site could not be fetched and the details come from search summaries.

Adversarial review: The vendor's own misconduct is established by two final regulator decisions: the FTC order and the Czech DPA's binding GDPR fine. It consists of selling users' re-identifiable browsing data while claiming it was anonymous. That directly contradicts the central promise of a privacy and security product, and it is relevant to a German and EU buyer. Under the weighing rules it stays RED even though the vendor paid and changed its practices. The positives are real but do not offset it. These are Gen Digital's financial strength, independent test results and a normal CVE patching cadence. The ongoing Dutch and UK claims and the SKU ambiguity add to the concern. Confidence is HIGH because the regulator findings are final, are confirmed and apply to this exact vendor.

findings.finding: A final FTC order (June 2024) found Avast and Jumpshot sold re-identifiable browsing data of Avast users to third parties from 2014 to 2020. The FTC also found this contradicted privacy claims. Avast paid $16.5M and is banned from selling browsing data for advertising. This is the vendor's own misconduct against the core promise of a privacy and security product.

The Czech DPA's final and binding decision (April 2024) fined Avast Software s.r.o. CZK 351M for GDPR violations. The regulator found the data transferred to Jumpshot was not anonymised, contrary to what Avast told users. This is a first-hand GDPR finding relevant to a German and EU buyer.
Follow-on litigation continues. The Dutch CUIC mass claim and a UK class claim are still referenced, while the US wiretap suit was dismissed on appeal in Oct 2025.

There is a steady flow of local privilege-escalation and parser CVEs in Avast products during 2025-2026. These were patched via updates. This is normal for a mature AV product, and no breach was found.
The product is real, widely deployed and independently tested. AV-TEST certifications and awards are recent.
The parent Gen Digital is highly profitable, with about $5B FY26 revenue.

Avast has been part of Gen Digital since 2022. Gen runs several overlapping brands (Norton, Avast, AVG, Avira), so consolidation of SKUs is possible. Avast One was relaunched in 2026 and Pro was reportedly folded in.
SKU overlap (Free, One, Premium, Business) and recent packaging changes make it unclear which product is being licensed. No end-of-life notice was found for the main products.
